evidence_items.summary: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without a type identifier and described only in plain text, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary structural representations. Starting from a pretrained four-step LoRA, structure-guided distribution matching renders in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling, while preserving the learned control. A block-causal variant extends the same design to streaming and renders 768p video in real time. To train the model, we build a frame-aligned corpus of 136K clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos. Experiments on an in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural representations show that SolarRenderer achieves state-of-the-art results across both, and generalizes to 11 unseen representations, including pose skeletons, drawings, and point clouds.
evidence_items.title: SolarRenderer: Few-Step Generative Reference Rendering

Companion sets: SRA-50 v2 and SRA-500 v2, built by the same pipeline with the same filters. Unlike the 50 and 500 sets, the runs here are not a sample: they are every run of the Metagraph 100-studies table that exists in… See the full description on the dataset page: https://huggingface.co/datasets/rsynk/rsynk-locale-benchmark-sra4571.

evidence_items.summary: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. These habits capture implicit user information that agents must infer across conversations. However, individual observations may provide only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies. Retaining past interactions alone does not ensure that agents can infer habits and apply them appropriately. We introduce HABIT-Bench to evaluate how well agent memory systems infer habits from weak evidence and apply them to later requests. We construct synthetic user histories from task-oriented dialogue data and controlled habit graphs. The histories span hundreds of sessions across food, finance, software, and travel. Four-choice tasks assess agents' ability to infer user habits and apply them appropriately. They include temporary exceptions, changes in habits, and suggestions that users have not accepted. Sampled tasks undergo independent human review. We evaluate eight memory methods with Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.3-Flash. The best-performing memory method achieves 33.61\% macro accuracy across the four domains. Performance remains limited even when annotated evidence is supplied directly. These results expose a persistent gap between access to past interactions and the ability to infer and appropriately use user habits.
evidence_items.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory

evidence_items.summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized the healthcare industry, particularly with the rise of healthcare chatbots. The healthcare sector has experienced significant digital transformation through the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly healthcare chatbots. These AI-driven systems can provide health information, initial symptom evaluations, and medical advice in a swift and efficient manner. While the promise of healthcare chatbots is great, issues related to reliability, privacy, and trust remain to be addressed. Trust has been shown to be one of the factors affecting the adoption and continued use of healthcare chatbots. This study seeks to explore the factors that affect user trust in healthcare chatbots and the effect of user trust on continuance intention. The research model is based on perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived risk, trust, and continuance intention, drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and social theory.
evidence_items.title: Improving Trust in Healthcare Chatbots

evidence_items.summary: This dataset contains survey responses from 1,000 Slovak enterprises across 24 selected criteria, together with reproducible calculations for assessing technological-organisational priorities and legal safeguards in responsible artificial intelligence (AI) governance. The Excel workbook integrates three information models (IM1–IM3) and a fuzzy multi-criteria assessment model (MF). It includes normalized indicators, expert-weighted composite indices, governance gap analysis, criterion-level diagnostics, fuzzy enterprise classification, and sensitivity analysis. The workbook provides adjustable model parameters and transparent calculation procedures to support methodological verification, comparative analysis, and further research. Illustrative expert assessments are distinguished from the original enterprise survey data. The resulting indicators characterize survey-based organisational assessments and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of legal compliance with the EU AI Act or GDPR.
evidence_items.title: Dataset and Fuzzy Model Calculations for Assessing Legal Safeguard Priorities in Responsible AI Governance: Slovak Enterprises

evidence_items.summary: This dataset supports the study Shape of Water and Daily Life: Measuring and Leveraging the Climate-Adaptive Potentials of Seoul’s Waterfronts . It contains shareable input data and author-produced processed data used to assess the heatwave and flash-flood resilience of 20 waterfronts in Seoul, South Korea, and the surrounding 5 km area. The files cover waterfront definitions, thermal relief, flood-buffer capacity, thermal-refuge accessibility, flooded mobility capacity, and combined resilience indicators. Some source data used in the study could not be included because of sharing restrictions; this deposit is therefore not a complete copy of all data used. See the README for the file inventory, data sources, processing details, and applicable attribution and license information. Related thesis: https://resolver.tudelft.nl/uuid:7aa7a4f9-82fa-4bdc-a00e-a845fbc49763
evidence_items.title: Morphology Based Climate Resilience of Seoul's Waterfronts

evidence_items.summary: Analysis pipeline, figure scripts, main figures, supplementary table sources, pre-specification documents and data provenance (SHA-256 checksums) for the manuscript 'Carriers of recessive disease are a mild form of the same disease' by Alexander Zentgraf and Christian T. Thiel. All analyses use publicly available summary statistics.
evidence_items.title: Companion repository: Carriers of recessive disease are a mild form of the same disease

evidence_items.summary: Abstract In migrating wildlife, plasticity in migratory behaviour is an important trait for responding to seasonal environmental variation and coping with anthropogenic change. Although partial migrants with a high level of migratory plasticity seem to be more robust to rapid climate change than full migrants, we have limited knowledge about the mechanisms behind migratory responses to the environment in partial migrants. Using a dataset of 691 fall migration seasons from 339 GPS-tagged partially migrant red kites ( Milvus milvus ), we quantify how two key environmental factors, deviation from the average temperature and food availability, affect migratory behaviour. Warmer than average temperatures tended to delay fall migration among migrants. Within a sub-sample of territorial adults, a supplementary feeding experiment revealed that supplemented individuals delayed migration and showed considerably higher residence rates (68%) than controls (43%) while the temperature effect was difficult to estimate because only few of the food-supplemented birds migrated. These results provide experimental evidence that future positive temperature deviations may affect migratory decisions of partial migrants mainly via enhanced food availability. This plastic, food-dependent migration behaviour predicts future increases in the proportion of residents in partial migrant populations, as well as increased resident occurrence in areas with favourable food conditions. This repository holds the data and code to generate the output described in the publication Witczak et al. 2027 (DOI: 10.1098/rspb.2026.2371). To replicate the analyses presented in the paper, use the file "REKI mig departure decisions.R", which includes the complete analysis and figures. This file reads in some prepared datasets that are stored in the 'data' folder and were prepared using the script 'dataprep'.
evidence_items.title: Data and Code for "Becoming resident in a warming world: Food availability shapes seasonal partial migration"

evidence_items.summary: A history-based predictor may outperform a fitted state model because relevant information was omitted, because the state model was poorly fitted, or because uncertainty was underestimated. We define predictive adequacy by a prespecified bound on excess population risk relative to a finite dictionary of complete predictors. Established empirical-Bernstein inequalities yield certificates for training-selected predictors and for selection within a finite class during evaluation. The guarantees require independent evaluation groups and permit dependence within groups. Pre-evaluation bounds on each pair's loss-contrast range improve on a generic bounded-loss baseline. Cosmology-motivated synthetic references expose underfitting, history censoring and false precision from counting correlated rows as independent. At Brier tolerance $0.01$, with 70 state candidates and nominal error $0.05$, a specified truncated-history pair's variance-inclusive population-moment planning curve crosses the tolerance at 13,464 independent evaluation groups with its verified range, versus 24,388 generically. These crossings are not power guarantees or universal sample-size requirements. With 16,384 total groups and 512 used for training, the range refinement raises evaluation-time class certification from 0 to 86 of 100 trials, while training empirical-risk minimization gives 99 of 100. Pair-envelope class selection reaches 100 of 100 at all tested allocations of 32,768 total groups. Gains depend on the contrasts that determine the bound, not merely on dictionary size. In a separate exact two-predictor reference, null-boundary error is approximately $0.029\%$ at 1,024 groups, below nominal $5\%$, quantifying conservatism rather than worst-case sharpness. These synthetic results concern specified predictors and observation laws, not autonomous dynamical closure or nonlocal gravitational physics.
evidence_items.title: Finite-Dictionary Tests of Predictive Adequacy for State--History Models

evidence_items.title: Dataset for the Development of an Adaptive Modular Robot for Autonomous Navigation in Disaster Environments Using Reinforcement Learning with Integrated Structural and Material Design

It covers 1,635 m of road captured with a Riegl VUX-1HA mobile laser scanner, about 57M points, manually labelled in CloudCompare into 7 classes: roads, lane lines, road markings, manhole covers, drains, cracks and road patching. evidence_items.summary: This dataset contains data on the performance of recycled polyamide (PA) dolly ropes compared with conventional polyethylene (PE) dolly ropes under sea-trial conditions. Sea trials were conducted aboard three commercial trawlers and one research vessel across the Bay of Biscay, Cantabrian Sea and North Sea. In total, the four vessels completed 429 trawl hauls and approximately 1,526 hours of towing under commercial and experimental fishing conditions, exposing the materials to a range of fisheries, vessel configurations, fishing grounds and seabed conditions. The sea-trial data include material loss resulting from material loss due to abrasion resulting from contact with the seabed. The field assessment was complemented by laboratory analyses to further characterise the materials and assess changes in their properties. These analyses included material weathering, optical microscopy, morphological analysis, chemical characterisation using ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, and tensile testing.
evidence_items.title: Sea trials of recycled polyamide dolly ropes

evidence_items.summary: The medico-legal report that documents torture sequelae for asylum proceedings is routinely delayed by forensic evaluation backlogs, yet the mental health consequences of that delay remain unquantified because randomisation to waiting is ethically impossible. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point difference at 80% power, and that designs with 8 or 16 clusters are underpowered across the entire effect range examined. The contribution is a design-level demonstration that the backlog question is estimable, and a specification of the cluster counts at which a credible emulation becomes feasible.
evidence_items.title: Forensic Trauma Evaluation Backlog and Mental Health Symptom Persistence Among Congolese Asylum Seekers: A Target-Trial Emulation of Medico-Legal Report Delays

evidence_items.summary: Java applications reach large language models (LLMs) through an integration framework, and rely on it to handle a failing provider: to retry what can be retried and nothing else, to wait as long as the provider asks, never to present a truncated answer as complete, and to record each failure in the application's metrics. We state these expectations as a six-clause reliability contract and measure Spring AI 2.0.1 and LangChain4j 1.21.0 against it with a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider: fifteen failure scenarios, synchronous and streaming, three repetitions. LangChain4j meets it in 47 of 77 applicable cases with its defaults and in 51 of 83 when configured explicitly, Spring AI in 72 of 77 and 76 of 83; both deliver a stream that ended without its terminator as a complete answer. We then place one implementation of the contract beneath both frameworks, at the HTTP boundary - an OkHttp interceptor for Spring AI, an HttpClient for LangChain4j, and a java.net.http transport for code without a framework - sharing a 725-line core that depends only on the JDK and the Micrometer Observation API. With it, all three clients behave identically and meet the contract in 90 of 91 cases; the remaining case is a policy trade-off between retrying a hung provider and waiting for a slow first token. Against a local model server the layer rejected none of 700 calls, and it adds a median of 32-217 microseconds to a call.
evidence_items.title: Consistent LLM Call Handling Across Java Frameworks: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark

evidence_items.summary: Language model benchmarks assign each question a single outcome from one fixed wording, even though the same underlying request can be expressed in many equivalent ways. We argue that the quantity of interest should therefore not be correctness on one wording, but the accessibility of an inquiry, which we define as the probability that a model succeeds across meaning-preserving formulations. The distribution of accessibility across inquiries reveals a structure that accuracy and existing best-, worst-, or average-case prompt scores collapse: how broadly a model's capabilities extend across inquiries and how dependably those capabilities can be elicited. Two models can have the same average performance while one succeeds across more inquiries unreliably and the other succeeds across fewer inquiries but more consistently, leading to opposite preferences depending on whether the task allows multiple retries until one success or when repeated consistent success is required. Across six benchmarks and more than twenty models, this tradeoff is common: for about half of the model pairs with nearly equal mean accessibility, which model looks better depends on whether one success across five formulations is enough or all five must succeed, quantities we call Access@5 and Reliable@5, respectively. For some pairs the two measures diverge significantly, by up to 10 points in opposite directions. Accessibility also reveals that scaling, reasoning, and prompt optimization can redistribute capability across inquiries in ways aggregate accuracy obscures, sometimes broadening the set of inquiries a model can succeed on while making success on them less repeatable. Accessibility turns formulation sensitivity from a nuisance into a measurable property of capability, distinguishing what a model can sometimes succeed on from what users can actually depend on.
evidence_items.title: Revealing what benchmark scores hide: Jointly measuring the breadth and reliability of LLM capabilities using accessibility profiles

evidence_items.summary: Applications of advanced heat resistant ferritic steels in boiler repairs require detailed information on the creep behaviour of welds made of various combinations of steels. The paper deals with the results of hardness and microstructure characterization of a dissimilar circumferential weld of 14MoV6-3 and P91 tubes after about 10 years of service exposure in a boiler operated at 580 °C and steam pressure of 10.3 MPa. The P91 tube (φ38x4 mm) was welded to the 14MoV6-3 tube (φ38x6.3 mm) using the GTAW (141) technology. Bőhler-FOX IN 9-IG (3Cr0.5Mo0.3V) wires were applied as a filler material. Microhardness evaluation after long-term service exposure revealed two carburized zones, values in these zones did not exceed 350 HV0.5. The slowdown of recrystallization in partially decarburized areas of the 14MoV6-3 and the WM suppressed the formation of soft ferritic bands along fusion lines. This phenomenon is related to the high thermodynamic stability of V(C,N) particles in vanadium-bearing low alloy heat resistant ferritic steels at temperatures below 600 °C.
evidence_items.title: Microstructure Characterization of a Dissimilar 14MoV6-3/T91 Weld after Long-Term Service Exposure at 580 °C

evidence_items.summary: Abstract We establish an exactness theorem for deterministic prompt-conditioned video computation with semantics-preserving state reuse, a lossless prompt–residual reconstruction theorem, and an explicit sufficient condition for at least 1000× hardware-cycle superiority over a specified comparator. These are conditional mathematical statements, not a proof that the current HKD implementation beats Runway or all state-of-the-art systems. Available empirical evidence consists of a single matched self-hosted CogVideo kettle pair: 659.412 seconds with reference validation versus 644.553 seconds with HKD validation and dispatch, a wall-time ratio of 1.02305. The decoded RGB hashes agree. No matched Runway generation, provider cycle counters, successful three-to-five-minute training run, or universal face/body fidelity result is available. We give the actual benchmark driver and the executable subset-sum verification code, distinguish counted operations from hardware cycles, and state precisely what additional evidence a stronger claim requires.
evidence_items.title: HKD Infinity for Prompt-Conditioned Video Production: Exactness, Conditional Cycle Superiority, and Measured Benchmarks

evidence_items.summary: Electromyography (EMG) provides a non-invasive means of decoding silently articulated speech into text, but accurate decoding remains challenging due to limited availability of paired EMG-text data. We introduce PhonoBridge, a two-stage framework comprising a channel-aware EMG-to-phoneme frontend and a large language model (LLM) backend for text reconstruction. The frontend is trained on paired EMG-text data that consists of channel-wise feature extraction, cross-channel fusion, and electrode embeddings. With phonemes as the intermediate representation, we expand the backend's training data by converting LibriSpeech transcripts into phoneme-text pairs without additional EMG recordings. To adapt the LLM to frontend noise, we introduce Error-Profile-Guided Augmentation (EPGA), which perturbs transcript-derived phoneme sequences according to error patterns estimated from frontend predictions, generating additional training pairs for the LLM. On the Open Vocabulary silent-speech dataset, PhonoBridge achieves 24.77% WER, outperforming the previously reported best of 28.27% on the same test split.
evidence_items.title: PhonoBridge: Error-Aware Phoneme-Mediated EMG-to-Text Reconstruction

evidence_items.summary: Community-based trauma rehabilitation programmes in post-conflict Liberia depend on donor funding cycles that rarely align with the longitudinal course of trauma-related mental disorders. The framework specifies three transition-timing parameters—transition abruptness, transition notice period, and post-transition service continuity—and derives the conditions under which each parameter alters the cumulative incidence of relapse. The analysis draws on published evidence on trauma rehabilitation financing, mental health service disruption, and donor transition in Liberia and comparable post-conflict settings to populate the framework's parameters and to identify the estimands that a competing-risks analysis would target. The framework proposes that abrupt transitions elevate relapse incidence through two mechanisms: interruption of therapeutic contact and erosion of community-based peer support structures. It further proposes that notice period length moderates this effect, with longer notice permitting both provider-initiated step-down and participant-initiated care-seeking. The contribution is a specification of the estimands, assumptions, and data requirements for a competing-risks analysis of donor transition timing, together with a set of testable propositions that link transition parameters to relapse incidence. The framework is intended to inform the design of donor exit strategies and the evaluation of their mental health consequences.
evidence_items.title: Community-Based Trauma Rehabilitation Funding Interruption and Mental Health Relapse in Post-Conflict Liberia: A Competing-Risks Analysis of Donor Transition Timing

evidence_items.summary: The BBG-TIC: Barometer of the gender gap in ICT studies (Barómetro de la brecha de género en los estudios TIC) is an interactive monitoring platform developed by the ALDABA-WIB (Women, ICT & Business) Interuniversity Chair, established by ALDABA, the University of A Coruña (UDC) and the University of Vigo (UVigo). The primary objective of this tool is to analyze the current status, academic performance, and longitudinal evolution of female enrolment in Information and Communication Technology (ICT) university degree programmes across Galicia (Spain). The platform integrates diverse heterogeneous open data sources. The underlying data model consolidates official academic records provided by UDC and UVigo (enrolments, new entrants, graduates, and credit performance) with regional non-university education statistics from the Spanish Ministry of Education, birth rate statistics from the National Statistics Institute (INE), and university dropout rates. This multi-source data processing enables multidimensional evaluation, including geographical distribution of new students, comparative academic success rates between genders, and generation-based cohort tracking from primary/secondary education to higher education. The software package published here contains the Tableau workbook (.twbx) and the comprehensive Technical and Functional Manual. The interactive and continuously updated version of the dashboard is publicly accessible at:  wib.aldaba.es/BBG-TIC
evidence_items.title: BBG-TIC: Barometer of the gender gap in ICT studies

evidence_items.summary: The timing of corroboration of survivor testimony in post-conflict legal archives has been proposed as a determinant of long-term mental health trajectories, yet the causal estimand is poorly defined and the design operating characteristics of any evaluation remain uncharacterised. The design parameters were a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5, and an intraclass correlation of 0.640; power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80% power. The framework clarifies the conditions under which archive-based target-trial emulation can support causal inference about verification timing, and identifies the cluster counts at which the BACI estimator attains conventional power thresholds.
evidence_items.title: Trauma Memory Testimony Corroboration and Mental Health Symptom Persistence in Rwandan Gacaca Archive Cohorts: A Target-Trial Emulation of Evidence Verification Timing

evidence_items.summary: Conditional cash transfers for trauma-affected populations in post-conflict northern Uganda typically tie graduation from the programme to a fixed calendar date, yet the timing of exit may interact with the trajectory of mental health symptoms in ways that current evaluation designs cannot detect. Because no primary observational data were available, the study characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and residual standard deviation of 4.5. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters would be required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power, a requirement that exceeds the cluster counts typically available in district-level reintegration programming. Graduation timing rules should be evaluated through target-trial emulation with explicit specification of the assignment mechanism, and that the before-after-control-impact design is underpowered for the effect sizes plausibly generated by conditionality adjustments in this setting. The contribution is a methodological framework and a power analysis that together specify the conditions under which graduation timing effects can be credibly identified.
evidence_items.title: Trauma Survivor Reintegration Cash Transfer Conditionality and Mental Health Symptom Trajectories in Ugandan Post-Conflict Districts: A Target-Trial Emulation of Graduation Timing Rules

evidence_items.summary: Supervision interval variation in trauma-focused therapy delivery is widely assumed to influence fidelity and, through fidelity, relapse. The assumption is rarely examined as a design problem: whether a stepped-wedge evaluation of supervision interval variation can recover the fidelity-drift-relapse pathway at the cluster counts available to district health systems is unknown. Power was estimated across 2000 design cells spanning cluster counts of 8, 16, 24, 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5, 8 percentage points. The analysis was designed to characterise the operating characteristics of the design rather than to estimate a treatment effect from observational data. At 80% power, 54 clusters were required to detect a 5 percentage point effect. The intraclass correlation of 0.64 dominated the power profile: at 8 and 16 clusters, power remained below conventional thresholds even at the largest effect size examined, and only at 32 clusters did power approach acceptable levels for the 8 percentage point effect. Minimum detectable effect declined steeply between 8 and 24 clusters and flattened thereafter. The results imply that district-level evaluations of supervision interval variation are underpowered at the cluster counts typically available, and that the fidelity-drift-relapse pathway cannot be reliably identified without either larger cluster counts or a design that reduces the between-cluster variance component.
evidence_items.title: Trauma-Focused Therapy Fidelity Drift and Mental Health Relapse in Malawian District Clinics: A Stepped-Wedge Analysis of Supervision Interval Variation

evidence_items.summary: The allocation of community-based trauma rehabilitation therapists in post-conflict Liberia has been constrained by the timing of mental health funding disbursements, yet the causal direction of the relationship between therapist density and recovery outcomes remains poorly identified. The analysis is framed as a methodological and theoretical contribution rather than an empirical estimation, because no individual-level recovery data are available. The instrument is constructed from the interaction between the timing of disbursement tranches and pre-existing administrative capacity, and the exclusion restriction is defended on the grounds that disbursement timing affects recovery only through its effect on therapist deployment. The paper also reports a descriptive analysis of a real DHS Program indicator on family planning messages at community meetings across 15 African countries between 2021 and 2025, with a mean of 29.733 and a standard deviation of 17.495, which serves as a benchmark for community-level health communication exposure. The contribution is a formal identification strategy that can be applied when individual-level recovery data become available, together with a set of testable propositions about the relationship between funding timing, therapist density and recovery.
evidence_items.title: Community-Based Trauma Rehabilitation Therapist Allocation Ratios and Mental Health Recovery in Post-Conflict Liberia: An Instrumental-Variable Analysis of Mental Health Funding Disbursement Timing

evidence_items.summary: Highway ramp merging is a safety-critical interaction for automated-vehicle validation because gap acceptance, longitudinal control, and lane-changing responses are coupled within a short time horizon. This paper presents a rule-distillation framework in which a large language model (LLM) serves only as an offline calibrator of a compact, interpretable rule expert: the model receives scalar replay statistics and proposes bounded updates of three rule parameters, every candidate is verified by closed-loop simulation, and the accepted rule expert is re-executed under legal-action masking and safety filtering to produce feasible demonstrations for an adversarial ramp actor, which is then fine-tuned by multi-agent reinforcement learning on a fixed scenario-replay library. On the training-distribution library, the distilled adversary reaches the highest evaluation return and reward-collision rate of the three schemes. This advantage only partly carries over to 150 held-out scenarios, where its reward-collision rate becomes indistinguishable from that of training from scratch (42.7% against 40.7%, overlapping intervals) while its evaluation return and its rate of successfully induced evasive responses remain higher. Against random-search and Bayesian-optimization calibrators evaluated under the same parameter ranges, score and simulation budget, the LLM attains a comparable calibration score with roughly one third of the closed-loop simulations and with a smaller run-to-run spread, but it is not a better global optimizer at the full budget, so it is best characterized as a sample-efficient and low-variance calibrator. The results indicate that verified rule calibration provides effective initialization for adversarial reinforcement learning within the evaluated simulation setting.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Model-Tuned Rule Distillation for Adversarial Ramp Cut-in Testing of Autonomous Vehicles

organizations: University of National and World Economy
evidence_items.summary: Abstract This paper examines whether decisions generated by large language model (LLM) agents can be represented by simple equations in an agent-based model of bank balance-sheet management. In a monthly leader–follower model, a stylised, predominantly deposit-funded euro-area bank chooses deposit rates, lending margins and the composition of bond reinvestment, while depositors and borrowers respond to these decisions and to economic conditions. The initial balance sheet is calibrated to selected indicators from regulatory disclosures. We estimate equation-based approximations of LLM-generated decisions and evaluate them against simulations not used in estimation. Across ten out-of-sample bank-year simulations, the final specification reproduces annual return on equity (ROE) within 0.31 percentage points and meets all fit criteria in seven; none of the deposit-run scenarios meets all criteria. In eighteen simulations with a second LLM family, the ROE difference does not exceed 0.71 percentage points, but only six meet all criteria. Against a market-pricing rule, the original optimisation model, and regression and nearest-neighbour approximations estimated on the same data, the final specification meets all criteria in more years and tracks liquidity most closely in deposit-run years. Instructions without behavioural guidance show that withdrawal magnitudes and fixed-rate borrowers’ price sensitivity depend materially on the instructions supplied; with customer equations estimated under neutral instructions, a two-month withdrawal episode no longer becomes self-sustaining. The results demonstrate a procedure for approximating and evaluating LLM-generated decisions within a defined simulation environment; they do not establish that these responses represent the behaviour of bank managers or customers. JEL classification: C63, C72, G21, E43, G28
evidence_items.title: Estimating Decision Rules from Large Language Model Agents: An Application to Bank Balance-Sheet Management

organizations: School of Management, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China
evidence_items.summary: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction is a crucial task to estimate the probability that users will click on items in online platforms. Recently, researchers have incorporated semantics derived from large language models (LLMs) into representations of users and items in a graph neural network (GNN) framework to facilitate CTR prediction. However, existing hybrid GNN-LLM models predominantly treat GNNs and LLMs as two independent components and suffer from ineffective modality alignment between graph and textual representations. To address these issues, we propose LLMs-enhanced GNNs for CTR prediction (GraphLLM4CTR), where LLMs coordinate message passing in GNNs by infusing layer-wise semantics into message updates and graph representation learning. Specifically, we design a multi-view contrastive alignment (MVCA) method to transform graph and prompt-based embeddings into modality-aware representations and achieve modality alignment through intra-view and inter-view contrastive learning. Moreover, we propose an LLMs-based message coordinator (LBMC) that projects graph representations into an aligned latent space and incorporates LLMs with learnable adapters to regulate semantic-injected graph representation learning. Subsequently, we present a hybrid-expert mechanism with gating networks to adaptively aggregate representations for CTR prediction. Experiments conducted on three public datasets (i.e., MovieLens-1M, BookCrossing, and Amazon-Sports) demonstrate the superiority of GraphLLM4CTR over state-of-the-art baselines in terms of AUC and Logloss, and validate the adaptability of MVCA to topological properties and of LBMC to text qualities, and the dynamic balance of the hybrid-expert mechanism.
evidence_items.title: GraphLLM4CTR: Large Language Model-enhanced Graph Neural Networks for Click-through Rate Prediction in Recommender Systems

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed academic research and institutional operations. Major LLMs, such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, Google’s Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, are now integrated into educational institutions at research and administrative levels. These LLMs go beyond summarizing text or polishing emails to include personalized learning, automated content creation, decision-making, and pedagogical integration. This chapter investigates the evolving role of LLMs in transforming the research landscape, particularly in academic writing, research management, pedagogy, evaluation, and ethical consideration. The research method is based on a systematic literature review (SLR) following PRISMA protocols, supported by bibliometric analysis and keyword-based thematic analysis of peer-reviewed articles from Web of Science and Scopus databases (2020–2025). Results revealed the existence of five major themes, namely academic writing and content generation, research evaluation, pedagogical integration, model comparison, and ethical considerations. The study highlights a sharp increase in publications since ChatGPT’s emergence, with thematic shifts toward education-related applications. Heatmaps across Scopus and WoS demonstrated significant trends toward real-world educational applications. However, ethical concerns showed strong growth, reflecting academic integrity issues. The keyword co-occurrence analysis also showed a dynamic research landscape with strong thematic ties to ethics, academic writing, teaching, and educational innovation. The overlay visualizations further illustrated the temporal evolution of topics from foundational concepts toward technology adoption, user experience, and collaborative learning. This chapter concludes by suggesting some recommendations to guide institutional policy and future research, ensuring an effective integration of LLMs in academic settings.
evidence_items.title: Transforming Research Management and Knowledge Creation With Large Language Models

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Clinical practice guidelines are central instruments of evidence-based care; yet, in many domains, particularly rare or complex diseases, multiple guidelines coexist and frequently offer conflicting advice. Existing strategies for resolving such divergences are often labor-intensive, opaque, and insufficiently reproducible. Objective This tutorial aimed to develop and demonstrate a reproducible workflow for transforming divergent clinical guideline recommendations and literature-derived white areas into human-reviewed Delphi-ready candidate items. Methods Following a step-by-step tutorial structure, we demonstrate the workflow using penile cancer as a worked example. The process comprises manual selection of clinical guidelines, a systematic PubMed search for literature-derived candidate issues potentially unaddressed by the selected guidelines, selection of 3 complementary large language models (LLMs), and execution of predefined prompts, multimodal recommendation extraction, semantic harmonization, and item-level guideline stance classification. The evaluative process combines a 3-LLM ensemble consistency check with an independent pre-Delphi appraisal by 4 penile cancer experts using a predefined 5-point suitability scale and acceptance threshold. Results In the worked example in the field of penile cancer as a high-stakes use case, the workflow extracted 157 clinical recommendations from 5 guidelines and consolidated them into 68 harmonized guideline-derived items. Stance classification identified 15 uniformly supported items and 53 divergent, ambiguous, or incompletely addressed items. In parallel, literature processing generated 95 harmonized white-area items, of which 9 were classified as true white-area items not addressed by the included guidelines. The final methodological output was a set of 62 human-reviewed Delphi-ready candidate items for subsequent clinical consensus voting.
evidence_items.title: From Divergent Guidelines to Delphi-Ready Items: Tutorial for Large Language Model–Assisted Guideline Harmonization Using Penile Cancer as a Worked Example

organizations: ASA College of Engineering and Technology, India
evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern marketing by integrating predictive analytics with generative creativity to enhance personalization, efficiency, and strategic decision-making. Predictive models enable data-driven insights through customer segmentation, demand forecasting, churn analysis, and campaign optimization, while generative AI introduces scalable content creation, automated design, and innovative product prototyping. Together, these technologies create intelligent marketing ecosystems capable of delivering real-time, context-aware experiences across diverse channels. However, challenges related to data quality, algorithmic bias, ethical concerns, privacy regulations, and system integration must be addressed to ensure responsible adoption. This chapter explores foundational AI techniques, key applications, creative advancements, and emerging research directions that shape the future of AI-driven marketing, emphasizing the need for transparent, ethical, and human-centric innovation.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence image generators are capable of producing digital images resembling traditional art forms by analysing vast datasets of such works; however, it is debatable whether these images are equivalent to the traditional art production process, which is based on patience, embodied practice and the master-apprentice relationship. This study aims to examine the ontological limits of generative artificial intelligence and the institutional regimes of legitimacy in traditional art within a dialectical framework, with a specific focus on calligraphy. The study adopts a qualitative, philosophical-critical approach grounded in a conceptual and comparative reading of the literature on the philosophy of art (Danto, Gombrich), Islamic art theory (Burckhardt, Yazır) and critical theory (Benjamin, Adorno-Horkheimer, Chul Han, Manovich). The findings are presented on two levels: on the first level, it is demonstrated that artificial intelligence cannot embody elements such as intention, the body, ritual, error and authorisation; consequently, it simulates not the calligraphic line itself, but only its superficial appearance. On the second level, the naturalness of this impossibility is questioned; it is argued that calligraphy’s conception of authenticity is itself a regime of legitimacy—historically constructed through the master-apprentice hierarchy and the institution of authorisation—which possesses exclusionary aspects. The study argues that artificial intelligence’s failure in calligraphy is not merely a technical or ontological shortcoming, but is also a consequence of aesthetic and political regimes of power that determine who is considered an artist and what is declared to be art. Consequently, generative artificial intelligence functions less as a threat that eliminates traditional arts and more as a critical mirror that reveals the tradition’s own boundaries and gatekeeping mechanisms.
evidence_items.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Generate Tradition?Rethinking Craft, Authenticity and Agency in Calligraphy through the Lens of Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: ABSTRACT This review scoped artificial intelligence (AI) in paediatric dentistry to summarize current applications and limitations. A comprehensive literature search was completed across PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and medRxiv/aArXiv. The preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA‐ScR) checklist was used for reporting the present study. Studies concerning paediatric dentistry and utilizing AI, machine learning (ML) or large language models (LLMs) were included. Two independent reviewers screened and three extracted data on AI methodologies, performance metrics, and clinical applications. Fifty‐nine studies were included. Computer vision studies ( n = 32) most often used panoramic radiographs ( n = 14), mainly for tooth detection, numbering and segmentation ( n = 10) and caries detection ( n = 9). Non‐imaging ML studies ( n = 18) primarily used clinical variables and questionnaire data ( n = 8) or salivary/biological samples ( n = 10). Accuracy ranged from 50% to 100%, with sensitivity reaching 100% in biomarker‐based studies. LLM accuracy varied widely (33%–96%). Computer vision and non‐imaging ML show promise for paediatric dentistry, particularly in the detection of dental structures and diseases, as well as risk stratification. Variable LLM performance underscores the need for standardized evaluation before clinical integration. Clinical Relevance AI‐based tools may support paediatric dentists by improving tooth detection, dental structure assessment, caries detection, disease prediction and risk stratification. Computer vision and non‐imaging machine learning approaches appear to have potential, but their clinical value depends on robust external validation, transparent reporting and integration into paediatric dental workflows. Given their variable performance, AI tools should be used only as adjunctive tools or a second reviewer.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Dentistry: A Scoping Review

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) showed greater accuracy than traditional machine learning (ML) models for classifying crime incidents, particularly when the LLMs were fine-tuned using policing data. LLMs also showed greater accuracy in understanding the context and meaning of written crime reports, making crime analysis more efficient and accurate. All artificial intelligence (AI) technologies used for policing purposes should be implemented cautiously, with human oversight, transparency, and safeguards against biased training data to prevent discriminatory policing outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Smart Policing

evidence_items.summary: Financial statements are prepared from trial balances that have passed internal-control checks and, for external reporting, have been audited before stakeholders rely on them. Converting this verified ledger into the views needed by investors, creditors, regulators, and management remains largely manual, causing rework, delays, and duplicated reconciliation. This study designs and evaluates an artificial intelligence (AI)-coordinated architecture that generates stakeholder-specific yet reconciled reports from a single governed trial balance. Following a design science approach, the architecture combines centrally configured accounting policies and KPI definitions, lineage metadata, account classification, anomaly detection, sequence forecasting, financial natural language processing (NLP), role-aware customization, and human-in-the-loop explainable AI (XAI). The prototype was evaluated on 15,000 trial balances for 500 entities (12,000 synthetic and 3,000 derived from public SEC filings) against rule-based, robotic process automation (RPA), and commercial generative-AI baselines. It achieved a line-item disclosure fidelity (F1) of 0.965, an AUC of 0.97 for misclassification detection, and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.8% for one- to four-quarter forecasts; in 250 simulated multi-entity scenarios, preparer effort fell from 38.0 to 4.2 person-hours per reporting cycle. Simulated stakeholder and auditor responses illustrate the expected gains in perceived usefulness and trust. Limitations include synthetic and statement-derived data, simulated rather than observed perception measures, and an unevaluated narrative-generation module.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Financial Reporting: Transforming Customized Financial Statements, Decision Intelligence, and Assurance Practices

evidence_items.summary: The penetration of artificial intelligence systems as general-purpose technologies into every aspect of social and economic life tests the adaptation capacity of legal systems to this dynamic process. This study analyses Türkiye's current position in AI governance and its future regulatory trajectory across three fundamental layers. First, although Türkiye does not yet have a stand-alone AI-specific statute, it evaluates how existing legal norms, such as the Law on the Protection of Personal Data, the Turkish Code of Obligations, and the Turkish Criminal Code, are applied to AI applications. Second, it posits that harmonisation with the EU AI Act (AIA) is not a mere policy choice but a commercial and technical necessity due to the Customs Union relationship between Türkiye and the EU. In this context, the nature of the AIA as a product safety instrument and its direct implications for Türkiye are examined. Third, the institutional transformation and the future AI governance landscape in Türkiye is addressed through the allocation of mandates between the newly established cybersecurity authority (SGB) and the Directorate General for National Technology and Artificial Intelligence (MTYZGM) under the Ministry of Industry and Technology. By providing a critical analysis of the recent legislative proposals submitted to the Turkish Grand National Assembly, the text emphasises the importance of Türkiye developing a unique regulatory strategy that fosters innovation while protecting fundamental rights. The study concludes that AI is not a transient hype but becoming a permanent and horizontal element of the Turkish legal framework.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence Regulation in Türkiye: Current Position and Future Trajectory
Handling class imbalance in high-throughput materials’ simulation data: a cross-validated ablation benchmark on an ab initio transport database

evidence_items.summary: Background. Knowledge-graph models can rank existing drugs for a disease, but their benchmarks mostly reward rediscovering known treatments, and their scores rarely come with evidence a researcher can check. We built OREVID, an open tool that shows a ranked candidate only when an evidence line supports it and reports how often each line was right on held-out data, and compared it with TxGNN on identical data. Methods. The graph combines PrimeKG, Open Targets, STRING and PubTator3 (157,822 nodes, 9.46 million edges). For each disease, 22 degree-weighted metapath features feed a LightGBM LambdaRank model trained with masked neighbourhoods. A candidate is shown only if it is indicated for an ontology-neighbour disease or for a disease sharing at least 3 associated genes (hypergeometric p &lt; 10⁻⁵ over the genes with at least one associated disease). The acceptance criteria for these rules were set in advance; the rules were revised on the hidden-treatment benchmarks and then measured on an external set of approvals not used to choose them. TxGNN was retrained with its official code on the same PrimeKG splits, and all tasks and predictions are released as OREVID-bench. Results. Zero-shot Recall@100 (mean ± SD over five splits) was 0.811 ± 0.042 for OREVID, 0.412 ± 0.042 for TxGNN and 0.358 ± 0.040 for a popularity baseline, with OREVID ahead on every split (paired difference with TxGNN 0.399, 95% CI 0.352–0.443, resampling diseases). On nine disease areas held out it was 0.617 against 0.237, ahead in all nine, although TxGNN had the higher AUPRC in five. Training OREVID without validation labels and excluding diseases where TxGNN outputs constant scores gave 0.809 against 0.421.
evidence_items.title: OREVID: Open, Evidence-Based Drug Repurposing with a Benchmark Against TxGNN
An interpretable synthetic benchmark for machine learning in low-strain pile integrity testing

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Characterization of Au(II) oxidation state remains challenging because d9 Au(II) complexes readily disproportionate to Au(I) and Au(III). We report the first high-resolution cryogenic photoelectron spectroscopic characterization of an isolated mononuclear Au(II) halide anion, AuCl3–, combining cryogenic anion photoelectron spectroscopy (PES) with relativistic quantum chemical calculations. The measured adiabatic detachment energy (ADE) and vertical detachment energy (VDE) are 4.63 ± 0.04 and 4.93 ± 0.04 eV, respectively. The VDE shows a near-plateau relative to AuCl2– upon adding an electronegative chlorine ligand, deviating from conventional superhalogen trends. Electronic-structure analysis reveals a high-energy Au 5d σ-antibonding frontier orbital, its unpaired electron axially localized in the Jahn–Teller-distorted C2v structure. Comparative relativistic vs nonrelativistic calculations confirm relativistic effects suppressing the VDE increase from AuCl2– to AuCl3–. The disproportionation reaction 2AuCl3– → AuCl2– + AuCl4– is downhill by 1.48 eV. These results connect relativistic electronic structure, photodetachment energetics, and Au(II)’s electronic lability and disproportionation tendency.
evidence_items.title:
Direct Spectroscopic
Benchmark of Isolated Au(II)
Oxidation State: Electronic Structure and Instability of AuCl3–

evidence_items.summary: Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) authenticate a device by its manufacturing variation. However, the cryptographic layer only verifies that a reading matches the enrolled fingerprint. It does not confirm that a live, honest device produced that reading. As a result, replayed readings, cloned silicon, and fault injection can all pass verification. We benchmarked our deployed machine-learning detector, UnifiedPUFNet, against six established architectures on 1~Mbit readings from 24 static random-access memory (SRAM) PUF tokens, withholding one attack family from training at a time. Six of the seven architectures reached an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of at least 0.999 in distribution, yet all of them degraded on attack families absent from training, and UnifiedPUFNet at one seed ranked replays above genuine readings. Replays disturbed few features, whereas clones shifted most features in magnitude. A dual-signal UnifiedPUFNet that adds a raw-magnitude input kept a mean held-out AUC above 0.99 on every family, although the clone test vectors differ from what a deployed verifier computes. Calibration and attack attribution failed on most held-out folds. These findings indicate that a raw-magnitude-aware detector is a practical candidate for PUF liveness checking, if validated on held-out attack families and thresholded at genuine-score quantiles.
evidence_items.title: A Leave-One-Attack-Out Benchmark and a Dual-Signal Architecture for Liveness Detection in Physical Unclonable Functions

evidence_items.summary: Does access to transaction-level records affect which forecasting method public-finance analysts should choose? To answer this question, we compare four forecasting strategies applied to a short, highly seasonal time series of child-benefit payments: top-down, bottom-up, data-enrichment, and minimum-trace reconciliation. Our application concerns monthly child-benefit expenditure in Republika Srpska (Bosnia and Herzegovina), where we have approximately a hundred observations of total payments, but more than a million observations of individual payments. We also consider four different ways to deal with the recurring near-zero observations typical of administrative payment data. Under an expanding-window design, where each model can only use information available at the time of each forecast origin, exponential smoothing performs best across every treatment, with minimum-trace reconciliation yielding statistically equivalent accuracy. Enrichment with features from microdata offers no advantage when those features must be known in advance, while machine-learning techniques fail to outperform the benchmarks. The choice of treatment for near-zero observations proves as important as the forecasting method itself. Overall, in the presence of strong seasonality and short time-series, widely-used forecasting techniques remain hard to improve upon, and more data only helps if it provides genuinely forward-looking information.
evidence_items.title:
From Microdata to Macro Forecasts: A Comparative Study of
Aggregation Strategies and Benchmark Models in Social
Protection Spending
