Governance issues were discussed more extensively in grey literature than in scholarly publications. Community participation, equity considerations, and formal governance frameworks were inconsistently reported. Conclusions AI is increasingly being applied in humanitarian contexts, but it is heterogeneously distributed across regions, humanitarian contexts, and emergency management. Greater emphasis is needed on real-world deployment, implementation-focused evaluation, participatory approaches, and governance frameworks that support responsible, equitable, and context-sensitive AI adoption.
evidence_items.title: From innovation to implementation: a global scoping review of artificial intelligence applications, governance, and challenges in humanitarian contexts

evidence_items.summary:
PURPOSE
Preoperative planning, currently performed by orthopaedic surgeons (OS), is essential for successful osteotomy, but is labour-intensive and error-prone. As such, there is significant potential in the use of automated artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to augment the abilities of OS in managing lower extremity pathologies in a high-volume task that demands high precision and reliability. The aim was to develop a deep learning (DL) system capable of fully autonomous planning a medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy (mow-HTO) on weight bearing anterior posterior (AP) long leg radiographs (LLR) and to validate its agreement with an expert-derived reference standard, its reliability and processing time of the DL model compared to expert OS on multicentric test data sets (two institutions).


METHODS
A total of 594 patients (age 41.1 ± 13.2 years, 182 female) who underwent osteotomy between 01/2014 and 01/2021 were retrospectively enrolled. Manual annotations for lower extremity alignment and high tibial landmarks were performed on AP LLR radiographs. The data set was divided into training (60%, n = 399), validation (10%, n = 59) and hold-out testing (30%, n = 136), with an additional external dataset (n = 100) for further testing. A DL system with twelve expert networks was trained to identify relevant landmarks for HTO planning. The DL model was then tested on fully automated planning of a medial open wedge HTO based on (1) the desired postoperative intersection of the mechanical axis with the tibial plateau (%-based) and (2) the desired femorotibial axis (°-based). Agreement with the expert-derived reference, reliability and processing time were compared with three expert OS using FDA-approved preoperative planning software on the test data sets.


RESULTS
For preoperative alignment parameter analysis, compared to the ground truth, human preoperative accuracy ranged from 0.13° ± 0.10° to 1.06° ± 1.4°, interrater reliability ranged from intraclass correlation (ICC) 0.84-1.0 and clinically acceptable accuracy ranged from 72% to 100%. Preoperative accuracy of the DL model ranged from 0.22° ± 0.18° to 1.04° ± 1.28°, interrater reliability ranged from ICC 0.93-1.0 and clinically acceptable accuracy ranged from 91% to 100%. For the planning of the osteotomy gap, compared to the ground truth, human accuracy ranged from 0.46 ± 0.65 mm to 0.5 ± 0.88 mm (%-based) and 0.43 ± 0.55 to 0.52 ± 0.75 mm (°-based), reliability ranged from ICC 0.9-0.96 and 0.95-0.97 and clinically acceptable accuracy was 93.6%-96.0% (%-based) and 89.8%-93.9% (°-based). For the DL model, the accuracy was 0.53 ± 0.63 mm (%-based) and 0.44 ± 0.53 mm (°-based), reliability was ICC 0.99 (both methods) and clinically acceptable accuracy was 98.1% (%-based) and 96.2% (°-based). The DL-model significantly and substantially outperformed the OS in intrarater reliability (0.88 vs. 1.0) and processing time for a fully automated alignment analysis (25.3 ± 0.8 s vs. 148.7 ± 10.1 s, p < 0.001).


CONCLUSION
The developed DL model enabled fully automated mow-HTO planning on AP long-leg radiographs with reliability comparable to that of expert OS while significantly reducing processing time and improving measurement consistency. These suggest that DL-based systems may assist orthopaedic providers by accelerating and standardising osteotomy planning.


LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
Level III, retrospective comparative study.
evidence_items.title: Multicentric development and validation of a fully automated artificial intelligence system for planning medial open wedge high tibial osteotomy on weight-bearing anterior-posterior long leg radiographs: The ISAKOS John Joyce Award 2025.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFRAI) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care.


MATERIALS AND METHODS
Diagnostic performance of CT-FFRAI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR.


RESULTS
In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFRAI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFRAI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P < 0.001 and P = 0.034). Net reclassification improvement for CT-FFRAI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively.


CONCLUSIONS
CT-FFRAI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.
evidence_items.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve across cohorts with different prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease.

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Objective: Triage and data transfer are critical to the medical management of mass-casualty incidents (MCIs). However, the chaotic nature of such events makes it difficult to classify casualties according to structured triage protocols. Furthermore, even when triage is implemented effectively, communication disruptions between the incident scene and dispatch centers can hinder response operations. The aim of this study was to present a drone-integrated system that enables non-contact vital sign measurement, remote triage, and real-time data transmission during MCIs. Methods: The system development process involved three steps: (1) developing the Vital-Sign Measurement Module; (2) developing the Triage Decision Support Module; and (3) developing the User Interfaces and Data Transmission Module to enable information transmission between dispatch centers and response teams. Within the Vital-Sign Measurement Module, heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), oxygen saturation (SpO2), and body temperature (BT) measurement algorithms were developed using the following techniques, respectively: video-based photoplethysmography (vPPG), analysis of thermal temperature fluctuations around the nose, a regression-based neural network approach, and heat maps and thermal thresholding. A pilot study was conducted under controlled indoor conditions to evaluate the accuracy of these algorithms. Results: The system can measure vital signs by processing drone-captured images, can provide triage decision support, and can transmit victims’ locations, vital signs, and triage categories to response teams and dispatch centers via dedicated user interfaces. A pilot evaluation of the Vital-Sign Measurement Module showed that the relative accuracy rate of the non-contact vital-sign measurement algorithms ranged from 86% to 99%. Conclusions: The system provides an innovative approach to improving medical response management in MCIs by enabling remote triage and monitoring. Its non-contact vital sign measurement, triage decision support, and near real-time data transmission capabilities provide an infrastructure that can contribute to faster response and improved operational coordination. However, further field trials and development are required to improve the robustness of the vital-sign measurement algorithms to motion, to improve their adaptability to changing environmental conditions, and to maintain high accuracy despite individual differences.
evidence_items.title: A Drone-Integrated Artificial Intelligence-Based System for Mass-Casualty Triage and Remote Monitoring

evidence_items.summary: Object: Motion artefacts remain a major limitation of routine two-dimensional T2-weighted turbo spin-echo (TSE) brain MRI, reducing diagnostic confidence and often necessitating repeated acquisitions. MoSAIK (Motion Search with AI in K-space) retrospectively estimates in-plane rigid-body motion directly from standard multi-coil TSE k-space. Without a motion-free reference, external navigators, or additional acquisitions, MoSAIK infers motion from k-space self-consistency violations and incorporates predicted parameters into model-based, motion-aware reconstruction rather than synthesizing corrected images. Materials and Methods: Selected complex coil data were represented as log-magnitude and phase channels. A decoupled convolutional embedding and Transformer encoder estimated phase-encoding-line-indexed rotation and two-dimensional translations. Training used motion-free clinical acquisitions with simulated motion; four held-out subjects were evaluated. Component-wise errors assessed estimation; SSIM and PSNR in silico and entropy focus criterion (EFC) in vivo assessed reconstruction. Results: Motion estimation errors were low for both rotation (MSE $<$ 0.2 deg$^2$) and translation (MSE $<$ 0.2 pixels$^2$), with Pearson correlations of approximately 0.96 and 0.94, respectively. In every in-vivo acquisition, more than 75% of slices showed information gain relative to uncorrected reconstructions. MoSAIK reduced visible artefacts while preserving anatomical detail. Discussion: Transformer-based k-space motion-trajectory estimation enables fast retrospective correction of standard clinical TSE brain MRI.
evidence_items.title: MoSAIK: Motion Search with Artificial Intelligence in K-space

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to 5G/6G network optimization, yet differences in empirical evidence, evaluation methods, and computational requirements complicate comparisons of reported performance. This scop ing review synthesizes 72 peer-reviewed journal studies pub lished between 2022 and 2026, selected through a PRISMA ScR-informed process from 893 records. The review examines empirical tools, AI/ML techniques, optimization domains, and operational readiness. Evidence classification identifies 37 studies (51.4%) using real-world or physical-testbed evidence only, 25 (34.7%) combining measured and simulated evidence, and 10 (13.9%) relying exclusively on synthetic or simulated data. Offline analysis was the most common evaluation setting, accounting for 45 studies (62.5%). Three principal findings emerge. First, empirical measurements improve contextual relevance, while simulation and digital twins support scalable experimentation but introduce validation challenges. Second, algorithmic effectiveness depends on the optimization objective, data characteristics, and computational constraints rather than model complexity alone. Third, predictive accuracy is more consistently evaluated than the network-level effects of optimization decisions. The review there fore introduces the six-module Evidence Fidelity and Operational Reporting (EFOR) checklist to improve evaluation consistency, reporting transparency, and operational relevance.
evidence_items.title: From Data to Deployment: A Scoping Review of Empirical Tools, Techniques, and Operational Readiness in Data-Driven 5G/6G Network Optimization

evidence_items.summary: Industrial artificial intelligence (AI) planning systems combine predictive models, optimization logic, controls, and governance rules, but improvement in the complete policy does not show whether one addition made an independent contribution or whether that contribution justifies its burden. We address this attribution problem with an observable evidence standard that separates opportunity to act, executed-plan change, operational consequence, equivalence, uncertainty, and operating scope. Using forecast-to-plan replay on Favorita, M5, and Walmart data, we apply the standard to heterogeneous planning additions. Three limits of single-indicator evaluation emerge. First, a composite policy can conceal negligible component contribution: one control changed only 15 of 681 executed plans. Second, changing execution does not guarantee stable benefit: the evaluated multi-period capability helped in several long-lead settings but was 7.6% more costly under tight capacity. Third, indirect evidence can prioritize review but cannot complete attribution. Independent runs produced different paths in 19 of 599 cases that a rule-based check predicted would be unchanged. Although a lower-cost diagnostic matched the full-evaluation winner in only 55.0% of cases, it selected an option within the $10^{-6}$ cost-equivalence tolerance in 79.5%; the remaining cases prevented the proxy from authorizing acceptance. These experiments establish capability-level contribution evidence; the organization completes the value decision by weighing it against implementation and sustaining burden. The resulting capability evidence record links the observations to validation, deployment scope, fallback, monitoring, redesign, and retirement decisions.
evidence_items.title: When Does an Added Planning Capability Create Operational Value? An Observable Evidence Standard

evidence_items.summary: Recent advances in nuclear medicine are reshaping the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis, as highlighted by the recent collection published in EJNMMI (collection link: https://link.springer.com/collections/igfdhcddjg). This commentary summarizes key insights from these studies, emphasizing the evolving shift from conventional diagnostic imaging toward a more integrated and comprehensive approach. Emerging developments include novel amyloid PET tracers, improved diagnostic accuracy with SPECT/CT, multimodality imaging strategies, and enhanced assessment of systemic disease burden extending beyond the left ventricle. There is also growing interest in longitudinal monitoring, pre-symptomatic detection, and the role of artificial intelligence. Together, these advances position nuclear medicine as an essential tool for disease characterization, risk stratification, and treatment assessment.
evidence_items.title: Expanding role of nuclear medicine in cardiac amyloidosis: insights from the EJNMMI collection

evidence_items.summary: Limited access to comprehensive sexual health education has prompted a need to consider the utility of alternative strategies, such as generative artificial intelligence (genAI), for delivering accurate and accessible sexual health information. Although genAI tools can generate health information, less is known about how perceptions of the source of information shape evaluations of content (e.g., human vs. genAI). The present study examined whether college students' perceptions of sexual health information differed based on source attribution. Participants (N = 266) were students recruited from a single university in the southeastern USA in 2025. They were randomly assigned to conditions in which they were made to believe that three sexual health passages that were identical across conditions (sexual communication, body image, and sexual pleasure and safety) were written by genAI, an academic expert, a community health professional, or a peer/social media influencer. Across outcomes-including perceived accuracy and clarity, warmth and helpfulness, trustworthiness, self-efficacy, and willingness to act-genAI-attributed information was evaluated less favorably than identical information attributed to human sources. For willingness to act, there were differences in source effects across topics, such that effects were strongest for sexual pleasure/safety and weakest for sexual communication. Findings remained significant after controlling for genAI familiarity/use and attitudes. Findings indicate that evaluations of sexual health information depend not only on informational content but also on perceived source legitimacy, suggesting that AI-based tools may be the most effective when paired with human guidance to support trust and actionability.
evidence_items.title: Generative AI vs. Human Sources for Sexual Health Information: Credibility, Trust, and Behavioral Intentions in a U.S. College Sample.

evidence_items.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has become a research focus in recent years, and has been widely applied in many fields. Due to its excellent natural language processing ability and its capability to simulate human conversation, the Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT) has attracted much attention from both media and academia. However, studies have mainly focused on the technical implementation of ChatGPT and its social impact, with few paying attention to the influence of its interface design on users. This study aimed to explore the effects of three research variables-response mode, polarity display, and visual avatar-on users' perceptions and experience of chatbot graphical interfaces. The study consisted of two stages. The first stage adopted a 2 (response mode) × 2 (polarity display) × 3 (visual avatar) mixed factorial design, which aimed to evaluate the effects of the relevant research variables on users' perceptions and experience. The second stage applied the Kano model to assess users' satisfaction with and importance ranking of the related research variables. The results indicate that Word-for-Word Responses received higher SUPR-Q and perceived Technological Sophistication ratings, whereas Full-Length Responses received higher perceived Human-Likeness and overall satisfaction ratings. Positive Polarity displays generally performed better than Negative Polarity, but in the human-avatar condition, Negative Polarity can enhance the sense of Technological Sophistication. The interaction patterns differed across outcomes. For user experience quality, Word-for-Word Responses received higher ratings under Positive Polarity, whereas Full-Length Responses received higher ratings under Negative Polarity. In contrast, for perceived Human-Likeness, Word-for-Word Responses received higher ratings under Negative Polarity, whereas Full-Length Responses received higher ratings under Positive Polarity. Polarity Display interacted with Visual Avatar in perceived Technological Sophistication, although the polarity comparisons within each avatar condition were not significant after Bonferroni adjustment. In the Human Avatar condition, Full-Length Responses received higher perceived Human-Likeness ratings under Positive Polarity than under Negative Polarity. The Kano analysis classified Negative Polarity as Attractive, Positive Polarity and Full-Length Responses as Indifferent, Word-for-Word Responses and the Iconic Avatar as Reverse, the Human Avatar as Indifferent, and the Robotic Avatar as One-Dimensional. Overall, among the evaluated interface configurations, the combination of Full-Length Responses, Positive Polarity, and a Robotic Avatar was the most frequently selected by participants. These research results provide theoretical support for the iterative development of AI chatbots, and have significance for the development of user experience in future GenAI application scenarios in daily life.
evidence_items.title: Interface cues in AI chatbots: Effects of response mode, display polarity, and visual avatars on user perceptions and satisfaction.

evidence_items.summary: Hypothermic preservation remains a critical bottleneck in heart transplantation, primarily due to the exacerbation of ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and tightly restricted organ viability windows. Addressing this global clinical crisis requires a departure from traditional monotherapies. This review critically appraises-rather than merely synthesizes-three multidisciplinary advancements: (1) preservation solutions supplemented with nanotherapeutics, with explicit distinction between proof-of-concept, small-animal, and clinically translatable evidence; (2) technological transitions from static cold storage (SCS) to ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) and nanowarming-assisted cryopreservation; and (3) bioactive compounds derived from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), evaluated through a SWOT framework that acknowledges phytochemical variability and the paucity of clinical transplantation data. We further examine the emerging-but currently nascent and largely speculative---role of artificial intelligence in perfusion decision support. We emphasize that these three domains are not evidentially equivalent: perfusion technology is clinically implemented, pharmacological and nanotherapeutic adjuncts remain predominantly preclinical, and AI applications in cardiac preservation are currently confined to retrospective outcome modelling, with no published closed-loop perfusion control in clinical practice.
evidence_items.title: Integrating emerging preservation strategies in cardiac transplantation: From nanotherapeutic frontiers to clinical translation.
Automated MRI Series Classification Across Heterogeneous Datasets Using Limited Manual Annotation.

evidence_items.summary: Neuro-symbolic artificial intelligence (NeSy AI) combines neural perception with symbolic reasoning, enabling logical reasoning. Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) is promising for NeSy AI, owing to its high parallelism and strong robustness to noise. However, the dense neural operations and memory-intensive symbolic inference in NeSy impose a severe"memory wall"bottleneck. Existing NeSy accelerators either focus solely on symbolic kernels or rely on conventional digital architectures, lacking a unified and energy-efficient hardware substrate. Moreover, exploring optimal hardware design configurations often requires costly trial-and-error. In this work, we propose UnO-NeSy, a unified CiM framework for optimizing NeSy computing. UnO-NeSy consists of UnO-CiM, an ultra-low-power NeSy architecture based on a homogeneous 2FeFET--2R compute-in-memory (CiM) array that supports both neural computation and HDC reasoning, and UnO-Sim, a cross-workload, end-to-end CiM simulator that models device non-idealities, neural quantization effects, and HDC execution behavior for accurate system-level evaluation. Built on UnO-Sim, we further develop an automated optimizer to identify workload-specific operating points under coupled energy, accuracy, and hardware constraints. By optimizing the operating configuration of the baseline 2FeFET--2R design, UnO-NeSy achieves $61.8\%$ higher energy efficiency and $38.2\%$ lower full-system inference energy. Across seven RAVEN configurations, UnO-NeSy achieves $96.2\%$ average reasoning accuracy under hardware non-idealities, demonstrating a practical and scalable path toward ultra-low-power NeSy hardware.
evidence_items.title: UnO-NeSy: Optimizing Neuro-Symbolic Computing with Unified FeFET Based In-Memory System

evidence_items.summary:
This article examines learners’ use of artificial intelligence (AI) with both languagerelated and subject-specific learning processes in the foreign language classroom. The development of critical digital literacy (#CDL), understood as the ability to critically assess and evaluate digital, including AI-generated content, is focused on in the reported research data, a video-taped double 
lesson of an upper-secondary advanced English course. In the lesson, learners used generative AI ChatGPT and DALL-E 3) to design their own campaigns for the promotion of gender equality, and discussed and reflected the appropriateness of AI-generated visual representations. The data analysis draws on video and screen recordings, group discussions, the plenary presentation and the subsequently initiated reflection. Focusing on a critical incident, the analysis shows how learners negotiate meaning by aligning with or distancing themselves from AI-generated artefacts, concomitantly developing, testing, evaluating and reflecting upon prompting strategies. In particular, the data reveal the learners’ critical engagement with AI-generated representations of gender in relation to diversity, equality, justice and intersectional equity as well as implicit and contested beauty ideals. Processes of interpretation, appropriation, emotional engagement and the act of developing and defending a position become visible as learners distance themselves from DALL-E 3’s stereotypical visual worlds and the underlying algorithmic biases of ChatGPT.
evidence_items.title: Die Förderung von Critical Digital Literacy im Englischunterricht am Beispiel visueller Repräsentationen von Gender durch künstliche Intelligenz

evidence_items.summary: Abscisic acid (ABA) was first identified in plants over six decades ago and is now recognized as one of the central phytohormones in plants, regulating growth, development, and physiological adaptation to environmental changes. In this Centennial Update, we use two influential ABA-related articles published in Plant Physiology in the early 2000s and discuss complementary advances in stress-responsive transcription and ABA biosynthetic regulation. We extend the Update from ABA-relevant gene discovery to recent advances in multicellular coordination of stomatal control. Growing evidence supports the view that ABA-regulated stomatal movement and gas exchange are coordinated across multiple cell types, including guard cells, mesophyll cells, bundle sheath cells, and vascular tissues in roots and leaves. We also highlight emerging tools to dissect this ABA-mediated multicellular network by using emerging technologies in single-cell and spatial omics, plant optogenetics, and artificial intelligence (AI). These advances will shape ABA research from single cell models toward multicellular collaborative networks for understanding plant-environment interactions. Together, this article links the history of ABA research with emerging single-cell resolution datasets and AI-assisted computational approaches, proposing a framework for moving ABA biology from well-established guard-cell signaling models toward a broader understanding of multicellular ABA coordination.
evidence_items.title: ABA and Stomatal Biology: From Transcriptional and Biosynthesis to Multicellular Coordination Across Cell Types.

evidence_items.summary: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but its impact on human diagnostic performance, the added value of visual explanations, and differences by reader background and experience remain uncertain. Methods: Using 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) images from two hospitals, we developed and externally validated an ensemble of three deep learning models after self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning. The diagnostic task used ECGs recorded within 14 days after symptom onset, regardless of reperfusion status. We conducted a four-phase reader study. Phases 1-3 compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and additional AI assistance. In Phase 4, readers evaluated a new ECG set after randomization to reference-sheet support alone, with AI predictions, or with AI predictions plus gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) heatmaps. Diagnostic correctness was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Exploratory analyses examined differences by cardiologist status and experience. Results: Development and external-validation cohorts, including healthy controls, comprised 832 and 95 participants, respectively. For Takotsubo-STEMI discrimination, external-validation accuracy was 0.914, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic and precision-recall curves of 0.970 and 0.984. Seventy healthcare providers completed the reader study. The estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 without assistance to 0.864 with AI assistance (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In randomized Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference-sheet support alone (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95; P<0.001), and Grad-CAM provided additional benefit (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25; P=0.033). Exploratory analyses showed greater improvement among less experienced readers; with AI assistance, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. AI-assisted readers remained less accurate overall than the model alone. Conclusions: An ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader accuracy. Visual explanations provided additional benefit, while experience-related differences highlight the importance of effective human-AI interaction.
evidence_items.title: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Aims Artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL), has shown significant potential for enhancing the assessment of echocardiograms in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of DL models and to identify factors affecting their performance. Methods and results A systematic review of the PubMed, CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted, yielding 16 248 potential publications. Of these, 160 studies met the inclusion criteria. Only studies applying fully automated DL networks to echocardiographic loops were considered. Performance estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. The studies were categorized into five distinct groups: prediction of disease or mortality, replication of established measures, segmentation of cardiac chambers, classification of chamber views, and assessment of image quality. High heterogeneity that could not be resolved was observed in studies focusing on cardiac chamber segmentation and classification. Model performance was influenced by a variety of different factors, including medical target and input characteristics such as video resolution, number of frames used, and total participants included during training. Conclusion DL models achieve high performance across various applications in echocardiography. In selected tasks, they may reduce reliance on expert input and support greater automation of echocardiographic workflows. However, further validation, assessment of clinical utility, and evaluation in real-world settings are required before widespread clinical adoption.
evidence_items.title: Deep learning-based echocardiography for cardiac assessment: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis

evidence_items.summary: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is the most common cause of vestibular vertigo, yet accurate diagnosis remains challenging without specialist expertise. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic algorithm for BPPV using video-nystagmography (VNG) recordings. A total of 1352 VNG recordings were collected from patients with posterior semicircular canal (PSCC) BPPV (n = 234), lateral semicircular canal (LSCC) BPPV (canalolithiasis, n = 188; cupulolithiasis, n = 58), and healthy controls (n = 224) at a single tertiary referral hospital, yielding 1738 signal segments (1312 nystagmus segments annotated by two otolaryngologists and 426 normal segments). Eye trajectory signals were extracted using a deep learning-based VNG eye-tracking algorithm, transformed into two-dimensional (2D) scalogram representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT), and classified using task-specific backbone architectures selected through systematic comparison under a patient-level data split. Ablation analysis showed that CWT-based 2D representations significantly outperformed raw one-dimensional (1D) time-series baselines. The final models achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values of 0.974 for horizontal and 0.961 for torsional nystagmus classification. For BPPV subtype diagnosis, recording-level accuracy was 0.935 for the PSCC and 0.938 for the LSCC evaluation; F1-scores exceeded 0.84 for all PSCC classes and ranged from 0.59 to 0.98 for LSCC classes, with canalolithiasis variants outperforming cupulolithiasis variants. These findings suggest the feasibility of AI-assisted BPPV diagnosis from VNG recordings.
evidence_items.title: Wavelet Scalogram-Based Nystagmus Classification for Automated Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo Subtype Diagnosis.

evidence_items.summary: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. However, the field has yet to reach consensus on its definition, technical landscape, and core challenges. To address this gap, this monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth. In doing so, it establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. Further, this monograph distinguishes physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins. It develops the foundations of physical AI across physics, control, cognition, learning, and reasoning. It reviews key methodologies, including multimodal perception, physical data and simulation, world models, embodied foundation models, motor-control systems, multi-agent coordination, and hardware-software co-design. Furthermore, it examines applications spanning robotics, manufacturing, infrastructure, scientific experimentation, and autonomous services. Particular attention is given to sim-to-real transfer, reliability, real-time execution, evaluation, safety, governance, and long-term deployment. By connecting perception, prediction, decision-making, action, and adaptation in a closed loop, this monograph identifies the technical challenges and research directions required to advance from narrow automation toward more generalizable physical AI and, ultimately, physical artificial general intelligence (Physical AGI).
evidence_items.title: Physical AI: Concepts, Techniques, and Challenges

evidence_items.summary: Emergency vehicles such as police vehicles, fire engines, and ambulances require a stable and efficient route optimization to reach life-critical events in the shortest times possible. However, the dynamic nature of urban traffic makes this ideal scenario much more challenging, causing critical life-threatening delays. Traditional civilian navigation systems cannot account for real-time traffic changes alongside vehicle-specific constraints, creating inadequate routing scenarios. This research presents the Constraint-Aware Real-Time Routing System (CARRS), a unified software architecture tailored for emergency coordination. The CARRS architecture is engineered to fuse together classical pathfinding algorithms such as A*, Dijkstra, and Bidirectional A*, with Constraint Satisfaction Problem methodologies. The Design Science Research Methodology is the research framework, and prototyping is the iterative process. The artifact was empirically evaluated using OpenStreetMap data for major metropolitan road networks, combined with simulated dynamic traffic scenarios. Performance metrics focused on route optimality, constraint adherence, rerouting responsiveness, and the potential for future system scalability. Findings revealed the system's capability to generate optimal routes for operationally relevant subgraphs in under 35 seconds, with incremental rerouting responsiveness below 20 seconds. Furthermore, the system achieved more than 90% adherence to vehicle-specific constraints, making the CARRS architecture viable for real-time dynamic routing requirements. This study delivers a routing platform that bridges artificial intelligence-driven optimization with software engineering operational compliance, presenting a practical transformative step toward adaptive emergency vehicle coordination in dynamic urban environments.
evidence_items.title: CARRS: A Constraint-Aware, Real-Time Routing System for Emergency Vehicles in Urban Environments

evidence_items.summary: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.
evidence_items.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs

evidence_items.summary: Multimodal rerankers are usually dedicated models: a vision-language model (VLM) is trained on retrieval data to score the candidates of a query. Scoring options is not specific to reranking. System One decision models such as Jev map a state and a typed question to one probability per option without generating text, and general models can make such decisions with little or no training. Reranking is one such decision, with the query and its candidates as the state and the candidates as the options. We therefore argue that a general VLM can serve as a multimodal reranker through System One decisions, and that decision tuning can improve its reranking. We ask a VLM one choice question over the top 16 candidates of a first-stage retriever and rank the candidates by the probabilities of their labels, read from one forward pass. On MMEB-V2 image retrieval, this choice scores 5.4 to 7.3 hit@1 above a yes/no question per candidate, and the yes/no question falls below the first stage. With the choice, zero-shot Qwen3.8-27B beats the supervised Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B on all three benchmarks and comes within 1.6 points of Reranker-8B on each. It matches Reranker-8B on MMEB-V2 visual documents (84.79 vs. 84.78 nDCG@5), at 1.1 to 1.5 times its latency. JEV-27B-VL, the same backbone tuned on text decisions only, improves page reranking by 0.6 to 1.1 points, with gains on most tasks (sign test, p <= 0.017), and leaves natural images unchanged. The zero-shot model is larger than the supervised rerankers and of a newer generation, so these comparisons are confounded; we discuss this and other alternative views, and the experiments that would test the position.
evidence_items.title: Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision

evidence_items.summary: Spatial reasoning asks a model to work out where objects are in 3D space, how they relate to one another, and how they move. Agentic VLMs have recently brought large improvements on such tasks by letting the model actively gather evidence with 3D perception tools instead of answering in a single pass. Even so, on many questions the tools return the right evidence and the model still does not arrive at the correct answer: the gap between model and tools, where raw readings become usable conclusions, is left unfilled. We present S-Agent 2.0, a spatial reasoning agent that equips an off-the-shelf general coding agent with a command-line perception toolkit, and we design the interface around one principle: help the VLM close the evidence loop: acquire scene evidence, remember it in a persistent scene memory, and interpret each reading in plain spatial language. This design keeps the full flexibility of a coding agent, and every reading it acts on stays grounded in the tools' geometry. On MMSI-Bench and ReVSI, the toolkit improves a strong open-source model, Qwen3.8-27B, by +13.9 and +20.5 points over the same agent without tools, and a strong closed-source model, Gemini-3.8-Flash, by +11.2 and +9.6 points. With the open backbone S-Agent 2.0 reaches 66.5 on MMSI-Bench and 82.3 on ReVSI, ahead of the specialized system SpatialClaw on the same backbone (62.6 and 74.5), and with Gemini-3.8-Flash it reaches 74.1 and 90.5 against its 67.0 and 79.7. Both tool gains shrink as the backbone grows more capable, but SpatialClaw's shrinks far more on ReVSI, from +13.2 to +2.7, while ours stays at +9.6. S-Agent 2.0 also works across different general coding agent harnesses, such as Codex and Claude Code.
evidence_items.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent

evidence_items.summary: Continuous flow language models offer a path to parallel generation with tools for control and acceleration unavailable to discrete diffusion, yet effective techniques for building them at the billion-parameter scale remain less established. We present Lafa (Large flow language model), a fast, high-performing flow language model scaled to 8B parameters in a data-efficient manner. Lafa is a blockwise flow model with causal attention on the prefix and bidirectional, asynchronous flow within each block. This design enables efficient training by adapting pretrained autoregressive (AR) models and fast inference via prefix caching and blockwise parallel decoding. We train Lafa at 0.5B, 7B, and 8B scales with fewer than 30B tokens, more efficient than previous diffusion models, and evaluate it on instruction following, reasoning, and coding, where the learned flow matches or surpasses the quality of AR and can be distilled into flow maps for one- and few-step generation. Notably, flow training preserves or even improves pretrained AR capabilities via a multi-token prediction effect, which we leverage in a self-speculative decoding scheme that verifies flow-based drafts autoregressively within a single model. This yields 2.54x the throughput of an AR model at comparable quality, outperforming multi-token prediction and discrete diffusion methods. Our findings show that continuous flows can serve as a scalable foundation for language modeling.
evidence_items.title: Large Flow Language Models

evidence_items.summary: For AI assistants to move beyond simple chat interfaces and reliably assist users with applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack, we need to improve their tool-use capabilities. However, existing tool use benchmarks are still limited and difficult to scale because they rely on human supervision or are too domain-specific. To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE ( T ool U se R elated T asks with L ong-Horizon E volution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents. The proposer is rewarded for difficult yet solvable tasks based on the solver's empirical performance, and the feedback generator summarizes the solver's execution traces for the proposer to exploit. TURTLE produces evolving, self-tuning test suites adaptable to different environment requirements, from supporting user simulators and dense document retrieval to interacting across multiple apps. Empirical results on AppWorld, $τ$-Bench, and AutomationBench using Gemma 4 31B-it show that the evolved tasks target the desired difficulty range (e.g., a 165\% increase in the percentage of hard tasks on AppWorld), increase task diversity (in terms of reasoning and simultaneous tool interactions), and elicit a broader range of failure modes than the original tasks.
evidence_items.title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use

evidence_items.summary: Unified audio-video creation requires a single model capable of text-conditioned joint synthesis, bidirectional cross-modal generation, and instruction-guided editing across both modalities. Existing methods rely heavily on paired corpora, which are scarce for joint generation and even rarer for editing. Consequently, they are spent learning single-branch generative and editing capabilities that abundant unimodal data could readily teach, rather than on the cross-modal coupling. Furthermore, prevailing systems apply a single shared noise schedule to both modalities, neglecting two critical limitations. First, due to the significant discrepancy in information density, video requires prolonged high noise to organize spatial and motion structure, whereas the sparser audio signal can settle earlier during the synthesis process, the dynamics a uniform schedule might compromise. Second, lockstep denoising leaves asymmetric workflows, such as conditioning on one modality to synthesize or edit another, untrained. We present UniAVC, which addresses both obstacles. It first trains each branch on unimodal dataset to full generative and editing competence, and subsequently dedicates paired data to exploit cross-modal correspondence. Modality-decoupled schedulers meanwhile warp the noise schedule independently from a shared timestep, while subtasks with one clean modality directly supervise asymmetric configurations. These settings respectively enable intent-aware editing, which preserves one modality intact while enlisting it to constrain the other, and post-inference self-refinement, which regenerates only an unsatisfactory branch against an accepted one. UniAVC thus spans multiple creation tasks from a single set of weights without task-specific adapters.
evidence_items.title: UniAVC: Unified Audio-Video Creation via Progressive Training and Asymmetric Scheduling

evidence_items.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated whole-body interaction with the physical world, yet collecting robot demonstrations at scale remains costly. Human demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, but existing egocentric human supervision often omits locomotion and posture, while embodiment differences and controller dynamics hinder accurate end-effector execution. We introduce HumanVerse, a 500-hour dataset of open-world human loco-manipulation pairing egocentric video with synchronized body and hand motion. Our human-to-humanoid pipeline aligns camera viewpoints and arm appearance, and refines motion references and controller inputs offline to reduce end-effector errors while preserving whole-body coordination. We validate the pipeline through zero-shot transfer to Unitree G1 on representative whole-body manipulation and long-range loco-manipulation tasks, without target-task robot demonstrations. Building on this pipeline, we develop λ_0, a humanoid foundation model for whole-body loco-manipulation, with robot-aligned human demonstrations providing supervision for mid-training. Increasing whole-body human data consistently improves downstream task progress. λ_0 achieves 90.0% success on SIMPLE and 62.5% across real-world loco-manipulation tasks. We expect this study to guide scalable whole-body human data collection toward humanoid foundation models for richer interaction with the physical world. Homepage: https://lambdahumanoid.github.io/
evidence_items.title: λ_0: Scaling Open-World Egocentric Human Data for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

evidence_items.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps. Feature caching reduces this cost by reusing features across denoising steps. Recent forecasting methods extend this idea by extrapolating features to skipped steps instead of reusing them. However, existing forecasting methods extrapolate the features they predict uniformly, even though the spatial-frequency components of these features change most at different stages of denoising. They also overlook that denoising progresses nonuniformly, so equal step intervals can correspond to very different amounts of change. These mismatches amplify forecast errors as more steps are skipped, limiting the achievable acceleration. We propose SpecKCast, a training-free method that forecasts the model output in the frequency domain. SpecKCast applies a 2D discrete cosine transform (DCT) to the output and tracks each coefficient with a lightweight Kalman filter along a band-specific time coordinate derived from the noise schedule. The filter tracks each coefficient's value and rate of change, and the transformer is evaluated only when the filter's forecast uncertainty exceeds a threshold. Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-14B, and HunyuanVideo show that SpecKCast achieves a better trade-off between acceleration and fidelity than existing caching and forecasting methods, reaching up to 6x speedup with less than 0.05 GiB of additional memory.
evidence_items.title: SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration

evidence_items.summary: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together. We introduce Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs), which use a single denoiser to propose parallel revisions and evaluate a candidate draft. We train the denoiser to reconstruct every token from uniformly corrupted drafts, teaching both preservation and repair. Its predictions specify revisions directly, without a diffusion reverse transition. Evaluation requires a different use of these predictions: confidence in an existing token reflects both contextual support and evidence from observing the token itself. Using the known corruption process, we correct for this self-token evidence to estimate how well each token is supported by the prompt and the remaining draft. Aggregating these estimates yields a cavity energy computed in one forward pass, without an additional scoring model. Each round proposes a revision, reads the completed candidate in its revised context, and retains it only if its energy is lower. Across Countdown, Sudoku-Extreme, and Maze-Hard, our method outperforms autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. With 6M parameters, DRLM reaches 44.4% on Countdown-5 and 93.9% on Sudoku-Extreme. The results establish complete-draft parallel refinement as an effective alternative to reverse diffusion for complex reasoning.
evidence_items.title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement

evidence_items.summary: We propose EMBER, a structure-based framework for TCR--pMHC binding prediction that eliminates the need for a predicted docked complex, and with it the placement error that dominates such predictions. Traditional structure-based predictors utilize the co-folded complex structure of the receptor and the antigen and interpret binding from its contact surface. Consequently, every downstream feature inherits any deviation the structure-prediction tool introduced. Methodologically, EMBER folds the TCR and pMHC independently, encodes them as SE(3)-invariant residue graphs, and compares their learned representations without constructing a shared coordinate frame. A relative pose is therefore not an input of the model, so placement error cannot propagate into the prediction. Computationally, EMBER preprocesses O(N{+}M) monomer folds where a complex-based predictor needs O(NM) operations. Experimentally, under epitope-disjoint evaluation with six retrained baselines, EMBER is first on every metric under all four folding tools, by 0.9 to 14.4% in micro-AUROC, 18.5 to 25.3% in micro-AUPRC and 10.6 to 24.1% in MCC. Its ranking is also up to 85% more stable across folding tools.
evidence_items.title: EMBER: Predicting TCR--pMHC Binding Without a Docked Complex

evidence_items.summary: Game world models have made rapid progress toward real-time interactive generation. Yet action control is still predominantly implemented as feature conditioning, leaving the model to learn from training data how each action should move the visual world. This formulation is poorly matched to a broad class of planar-camera worlds, such as top-down and isometric games. In these worlds, player motion induces a geometrically well-defined planar camera displacement. We observe that the key to spatially consistent control in such worlds is to represent the effect of each action directly in world coordinates. To this end, we introduce ActionRoPE, a parameter-free action interface that converts action-driven camera displacement into world-coordinate rotary positions. As a result, tokens corresponding to the same world location retain the same positional address across time. These world coordinates further expose a spatial asymmetry in generation: regions covered by the initial observation are geometrically known, while newly revealed regions remain to be synthesized. We therefore propose Coordinate-Conditioned Noise Scheduling (CNS), which assigns token-wise denoising schedules according to this known-new structure. It allows observed regions to stabilize earlier, while new content is generated with reference to them. Compared with four representative action-conditioning mechanisms, our approach follows the commanded motion more faithfully and reduces the revisit drift by 66% over the strongest baseline. The same interface transfers across video backbones from 1.3B to 33B parameters and to out-of-distribution scenes. Project Page: https://teawhite.cn/ActionRoPE/
evidence_items.title: ActionRoPE: action as coordinates for spatially consistent control in planar-camera game world models

evidence_items.summary: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories. KronLSTM extends the xLSTM family with a memory-revision mechanism that corrects targeted associations while modifying the memory only along a single direction in matrix space. This minimally invasive memory revision reduces interference with previously stored information compared with delta-rule updates, making it particularly well suited for long-context language modeling. The resulting memory dynamics can be mathematically described as a Markov chain that converges to a steady-state distribution, while the expected norm of the memory matrix remains uniformly bounded throughout the entire input sequence. Hence, KronLSTM ensures stable memory dynamics without requiring additional normalization and stabilization mechanisms for the memory state. Experiments show that KronLSTM is competitive with, and often outperforms, existing linear attention architectures, including models of the (Gated) DeltaNet family, with particularly strong performance on long context benchmarks. These results establish the Kronecker Delta Rule as an effective and analytically tractable foundation for stable associative memory in recurrent linear attention architectures. Our code (https://github.com/NX-AI/KronLSTM) and models (https://huggingface.co/collections/NX-AI/kronlstm) are open-source.
evidence_items.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention

evidence_items.summary: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) is designed to support flexible representation sizes by jointly optimizing nested prefixes. While effective, this design lacks an explicit constraint to ensure that the leading portion provides a suitable compact encoding. To address this, we propose SpecMRL, which reorganizes the feature space to enable more effective prefix readout. Specifically, we extend MRL with a parameter-derived spectral basis organized with feature importance. SpecMRL otherwise follows standard MRL, with prefix readout performed in the learned spectral space. Experiments on MTEB show that SpecMRL outperforms MRL at all evaluated reduced dimensions, with larger gains under more aggressive compression. These results suggest that the learned spectral basis better prioritizes informative directions, enabling more effective representation compression. Notably, SpecMRL extends the performance frontier of MRL, surpassing full-dimensional MRL with only half the embedding dimensions.
evidence_items.title: SpecMRL: Redesign Matryoshka Representation Learning within Parametric Spectrum

evidence_items.summary: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2times less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs. 41.0 gFD) with 275times less pretraining compute. Controlled experiments show that text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation. Halcyon also learns image captioning by replacing caption dropout with I2T supervision, maintaining competitive T2I generation quality under the same pretraining budget. We show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining. Code and models are available at https://cs.stanford.edu/~keshik/halcyon
evidence_items.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining

evidence_items.summary: Brain encoding models aim to predict neural responses to stimuli. The most widely used approach fits readouts from frozen pretrained backbones. Using neural data to train large models from scratch or fully fine-tune them after task-pretraining has proven difficult because neural data is costly and limited. We show that parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enables us to effectively adapt very large pretrained backbones for brain encoding with a small number of trainable parameters. To make it computationally practical, we exploit the backbone's causal structure to predict multiple timepoints in a single pass instead of using sliding windows, significantly reducing feature-extraction cost. This enables efficient fine-tuning of multimodal backbones with up to 104B parameters, the largest model adapted for brain encoding to our knowledge. Trained with a low-rank adapter (LoRA) and a lightweight readout, our approach consistently improves brain encoding performance across nine diverse multimodal backbones. On the same Qwen3-Omni backbone as the prior state-of-the-art (SoTA), our method BrainLoRA achieves the best published performance on the Algonauts 2025 Challenge. We also show the adapted multimodal backbones remain interpretable: modality attribution recovers the canonical sensory topography that prior work often obtains by construction from separate unimodal encoders, and neural adaptation increases the contribution of audio inputs and cross-modal mixing within the backbone. To scale out the number of adapted models, we develop a multi-LoRA kernel that accelerates joint training of multiple LoRAs on a shared backbone. This enables an ensemble of 200+ adapted models that ranks first on the public Algonauts post-challenge leaderboard at the time of writing. Together, our results highlight PEFT as an efficient and powerful paradigm for brain encoding.
evidence_items.title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
